newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Novartis to consolidate Swiss drugs output.
newsitem.headline: Novartis to consolidate Swiss drugs output.

text.p: Novartis said on Tuesday it would concentrate pharmaceutical production in fewer factories in Europe in a move that would eliminate up to 500 jobs in Switzerland over the next three to four years.
All of them were included in the estimated 3,000 jobs Novartis had already announced would be cut as a result of the merger between Ciba Geigy Ag and Sandoz AG SANZ.S, it said in a statement.

Novartis said it would invest considerably to expand further the manufacture of active phamaceutical substances in its present Swiss facilities. Production of dosage forms would be integrated into European production systems.

"In accordance with the guidelines developed for this concept, pharmaceutical production will be concentrated in fewer factories, with the individual plants specialising in particular formulations (e.g. tablets, ampoules, ointments, etc)," it said.

Swiss output would be concentrated the the Stein facility. Corresponding operations at Basle St Johann would be relocated to Stein, other facilities in the region and Italy, it said. Basle St Johann would remain a logistics centre.

It said the move should produce significant productivity gains. Fewer than 500 jobs might go if growth developed dynamically as expected, it said, adding that the cuts would come largely via attrition, internal job changes and early retirement.
"The necessary steps have already been initiated for employees affected in 1997," it said.
